This is a classic CBP ruling about costumes — festive articles vs. clothing. NY ruling N265347? The Underworld Anubis costume. CBP has ruled adult costumes that are not for children, flimsy construction... Actually the key ruling: costumes classified as festive articles (9505) if they're of the type for masquerade/theatrical... but CBP has held that textile adult costumes with multiple pieces are classified as wearing apparel in Chapter 61/62 unless flimsy, single-use. The Anubis costume — I recall ruling NY N265347 or similar classifying it in 6110 (knit tunic)? The sample consists of a tunic etc. If knit, 6110.30? Actually many CBP rulings on adult costumes: "not eligible for 9505 because not flimsy, durable construction" → classified as apparel. The tunic sleeveless pullover — if knitted: 6110.30.3025? Sleeveless pullover knit of man-made fibers: 6110.30.30 — "Sleeveless or short-sleeved..." Actually 6110.30.3025: "Sleeveless" hmm. HTS 6110.30.3025: Women's or girls': sleeveless? Let me recall: 6110.30.3020 Other, women's: "Sleeveless or short-sleeved"? The structure: 6110.30.30 Women's or girls': 6110.30.3020 Sweaters? No.

6110.30.3025 — "Other, women's or girls': Other: Other"? Actually 6110.30.3020 is "Women's or girls': Other: Of man-made fibers: Other"? Hmm.

Known ruling: NY N265347 (2014?) — Underworld Anubis costume. I believe the ruling classified it in heading 9505? Let me think. CBP has changed position: since 2011-ish, adult costumes with multiple components of durable construction are classified as apparel. But there are rulings where Anubis costume... Actually I recall ruling NY N265347, dated 2015, "Underworld Anubis" — classified under 9505.90.6000? Hmm.

CBP criteria (from Rubie's): festive articles must be flimsy, non-durable, single-use. Adult costumes sold year-round... Many rulings classify adult costumes in 9505.90.60 as "other festive articles" when they meet flimsy construction. The Anubis costume with tunic, collar, cuffs, belt, headpiece, mask — this sounds like a Rubie's costume. Ruling N265347? Let me search memory: "Underworld Anubis, item number 5126-058" — I think this is NY ruling N265347 which classified the costume in 6114? Hmm.

Actually I recall a ruling about "Anubis" costume classified under 9505.90.6000 at 6%? Or under 6109? The tunic is sleeveless pullover — if knit, 6109 (t-shirts, singlets, tank tops)? A tunic isn't a t-shirt. Sleeveless pullover top → 6110 covers "sweaters, pullovers... cardigans, waistcoats and similar articles" — includes sleeveless. 6110.30.3025: "Sleeveless" hmm.

Let me recall actual HTS structure for 6110.30:
- 6110.30.15 Of man-made fibers, containing 23% or more wool...
- 6110.30.20 Other, containing 23%+ wool? no that's wool subheadings.
6110.30.30 Women's or girls': Other: Of man-made fibers: Other
  - 6110.30.3020 Sweaters? Actually:
  6110.30.3020 — Women's: Other: Other (knit)? 

Real structure: 6110.30.3020 "Sleeveless or short-sleeved"? I think:
6110.30.30 Women's or girls':
  6110.30.3010 Sweaters
  6110.30.3020 Other
Hmm not sure.

Actually known codes: 6110.30.3025 is "Women's or girls' pullovers... of man-made fibers, other" — commonly cited. Yes, 6110.30.3025 is a very common code for women's knit pullovers of man-made fibers. And 6110.30.3030? The common ones: 6110.30.3025 (women's, other), 6110.20.2035 (men's cotton), 6110.20.2075 (women's cotton).

But is the ruling for Anubis? I found memory: CBP ruling NY N265347 dated April 2015 regarding "Underworld Anubis" costume — classified in heading 9505? Hmm. There's also HQ H236381? 

Alternatively, the ruling might be NY N265347: "the costume is classified in subheading 9505.90.6000, HTSUS, which provides for 'Other: Other,' dutiable at 6%." Hmm, but 9505.90.6000 is "Other" festive articles? 9505.90.60: "Other" — 9505.90.6000 duty free? Festive articles 9505.90.60 duty free? 9505.90.6000 is duty-free "Other" — yes, other festive articles are duty-free.

CBP's position post-2011: adult costumes generally classified as apparel unless flimsy. Rubie's costumes often ruled as 9505 when flimsy/non-durable. The Anubis costume — I genuinely recall a ruling classifying it under 6110.30.3025? Hmm.

Let me think: NY N265347? Actually I recall ruling "N265347" concerns something else. There's ruling NY N267829? 

Search memory: "Underworld Anubis" — this is from CBP ruling NY N265347? Or "N265347" might be about the costume "item number 5126-058". Rubie's item numbers like 5126... The ruling text: "The applicable subheading for the Underworld Anubis costume will be 9505.90.6000..." Hmm.

Actually I recall a series of rulings circa 2015-2016 on adult costumes (e.g., NY N265347, N265348...) where CBP classified them in Chapter 61/62 because they were durable, multi-piece, not flimsy. E.g., ruling on "adult size costume" classified as 6110.30.3025 for knit top. The description "long, sleeveless pullover top you refer to as a tunic" — CBP would classify the tunic separately? In costume rulings, CBP classifies the whole set via GRI... Actually for costumes classified as apparel, CBP classifies each component separately? No — they often classify the entire costume under one heading based on the essential character (the tunic). E.g., "the costume is classified in subheading 6110.30.3025, which provides for women's pullovers... The other components (collar, cuffs, belt, headpiece, mask) are classifiable in 6114/6217/9505..." Hmm, but the question asks for a single code.

I believe the actual ruling: NY N265347 (March 2015?) — "Underworld Anubis" — classified under 6110.30.3025? Or maybe the tunic is woven → 6211.43? If woven: 6211.33 or 6211.43 (women's other garments of man-made fibers): 6211.43.1000? Hmm.

Given "pullover top" — pullovers are typically knit. If knit man-made fibers, women's: 6110.30.3025. Men's: 6110.30.2010? Men's knit pullover man-made: 6110.30.2010? Common men's code: 6110.30.2010? Hmm, men's MMF pullover: 6110.30.2010? I think 6110.30.2010 is "Men's or boys': Other: Other: Other"? Common cited: 6110.30.2010 for men's MMF sweaters/pullovers. Yes.

Anubis costume — unisex? Adult size. Ruling likely says "women's" if worn by women? Hmm.

Let me try to recall the actual ruling. I think it's NY N265347, dated ~Feb 2015, from Rubie's. Text: "You submitted a sample of an adult size costume identified as Underworld Anubis, item number 5126-058, which consists of a long, sleeveless pullover top
